limits: Identification rests on three bands. With one fitted frequency scale per candidate, three matches can occur by chance, so the ranking is only moderately discriminating. The second candidate's score (0.74) is not negligible in raw score, and it is excluded only by missing strong predicted modes.

The skill has no curated literature mode table or material note for InOCl/ClInO (lookup_reference_modes returned 'no literature table'). The mode labels Ag come from the DFT entry, not from measured polarization. The skill has no ClInO-specific layer, strain, or doping relations, so none are reported.

No polarization data was supplied (single spectrum), so the Ag symmetry is not tested. In backscattering along the layer normal, Ag modes are expected in xx/yy geometries, which is consistent with the three bands but does not prove it.

No Si line is present in the 60-1100 cm-1 window and no substrate was given (fit run with substrate 'none'). The spectrum therefore has no internal calibration check, and absolute positions carry the instrument calibration uncertainty, which is not quantified here.

The spectrum starts at 60 cm-1, so modes below 60 cm-1 cannot be assessed. Above 400 cm-1 the spectrum shows only a sloping background with no reported bands. A lower-SNR refit (--min-snr 3) finished in the background and returned the same three main bands (155.66, 299.49, 354.12 cm-1; widths slightly larger for 299.5 cm-1), plus two features I do not accept as peaks: 329.9 cm-1 (height error exceeds height, unresolved) and 889.4 cm-1 (about 8 cm-1 from the removed 897.5 cm-1 spike, likely spike residue or noise). Weak structure near 382 cm-1 (SNR about 2) is not significant.
Resonance and laser-energy effects were not evaluated. The 532 nm laser, 295 K temperature, and unknown substrate and polarization geometry are assumed, not measured.
